units.title: Two bisectors give equal segments around an incircle contact
units.statement: Let an incircle touch BC,CA,AB at D,E,F of an acute triangle ABC. Put x=AF=AE, y=BF=BD, z=CE=CD, so AB=x+y. If DF bisects angle ADK and EF bisects angle BEL for K,L on AB, angle-bisector ratios give AL=x²/(x+y) and AK=x+xy/(x+y). Hence △ALE is similar to △AEB by the included angle at A and adjacent side ratio AL/AE=AE/AB, while FK=FL=xy/(x+y).
steps: Replace the six contact segments by three tangent lengths
Apply the angle-bisector theorem in triangles ADK and BEL
Compare AL, AF, and AK on AB
